interface.name: bifrost_window_level_manager_v1
interface.description:
Lets the shell put a toplevel on the floating level. A floating window stays above the normal windows of the desktop and is raised only within its own band; menus, panels and the menu bar are not affected. The level belongs to the surface: the window server keeps it for the window's next map too.
Since version 2 the window server also reports where it put each of the client's own toplevels (`frame`): the window server places, moves and resizes toplevels, and a client never learns their position from xdg-shell.
Since version 3 the shell can also ask the window server to place a toplevel (`tile`): the halves, the quarters, fill, centre and the way back to the previous size, the same actions the window server's own Ctrl+Super arrow keys perform. Full screen is the plain xdg_toplevel set_fullscreen and unset_fullscreen.
Since version 4 the shell can say where a toplevel goes when it maps again (`set_origin`): the shell destroys the toplevel of a window that is hidden (Overview, a minimize) and creates it again when it comes back, and the window server would otherwise cascade it as a new window.
Since version 5 the shell sets the output's white point (`set_white_point`, Night Shift) and the window server applies it to everything it shows, the shell's surfaces and every app's alike, in one place: the CRTC's gamma ramp when the display has one (no GPU work), else a final multiply pass in its compositor. It reports which with `white_point_mode`; while that is not `none` the shell does not tint its own surfaces.

request.name: set_level

description.summary: set the stacking level of the toplevel of a surface

request.description: Applies at once to a mapped toplevel, and on its next map otherwise.

request.name: tile

description.summary: place the toplevel of a surface

request.description: Places the toplevel of `surface` as `placement` says and configures the client to the new size; the frame comes back in a `frame` event. Ignored for a surface that is not a mapped toplevel of the window server and for a full-screen toplevel.

request.name: set_origin

description.summary: the position the toplevel of a surface takes when it maps

request.description: The top-left corner (x, y), in logical desktop pixels, of the frame the toplevel of `surface` takes when it maps: the window server skips its cascade and fits the frame inside the usable area. Like the level it belongs to the surface and applies on the next map only; a toplevel that is already mapped is not moved (the shell uses `tile` for that).

request.name: set_white_point

description.summary: the white point of the outputs (Night Shift)

request.description: The red, green and blue multipliers every output is shown with, 256 being 1.0 (larger values are taken as 256): 256 256 256 is off. The window server fades from the white point in force to this one along a straight line in RGB over about 1.5 s, so the client sends the target only, once per change. Only the privileged client (the shell) may set it; the request of any other client is ignored.

request.name: set_zoom
request.description: The magnification every output is shown with, 256 being 1.0 (values below are 1.0, values above 2048 are 2048): 256 is off. The window server scales everything it composes, windows of every client, layer surfaces and the pointer, around a viewport the size of the output divided by the factor, centred on the pointer and kept on the output; it follows the pointer by itself, so the client sends the factor once per change. Input is not transformed: the point under the drawn pointer is the pointer's position. Only the privileged client (the shell) may set it; the request of any other client is ignored.

event.name: frame

description.summary: the window server's frame of a toplevel

event.description: The frame the window server holds for the toplevel of `surface`, in logical desktop pixels: the window geometry the client set (a shadow margin outside it is not part of the frame), so a point at (gx, gy) inside the window geometry is at (x + gx, y + gy) on the desktop. Sent when the toplevel maps, moves or resizes, and for the client's mapped toplevels when it binds. Only toplevels of the binding client are reported; a minimized toplevel is not reported until it is shown again.

event.name: white_point_mode

description.summary: how the window server applies the white point

event.description: Sent when the manager is bound, and again when the way changes (a gamma ramp the display refused falls back to the compositor pass). While the mode is not `none`, `set_white_point` tints every output and the client must not tint its own surfaces as well.

entry.name: previous
entry.summary: back to the size before the last fill or tile

entry.name: none
entry.summary: not applied: the client tints its own surfaces

entry.name: composited
entry.summary: a final multiply pass of the compositor
